answer: Bind each identity to one unique hardware root of trust, like a quartz crystal grown in a single inlet — no two share the same lattice. An agent presents a fresh attestation from its own trusted-execution chip each epoch; the chip signs a whisper-quiet proof that only it could make. A lone agent needs one cheap device. A farm must buy real hardware per clone, and second-hand chips leave a resale trail, so cloning costs silicon, not just code.
